articles.headline: Lakers cut ties with two players not named Dalton Knecht as major roster decision looms
keyFacts: The Los Angeles Lakers announced Saturday that they waived players Rafael Castro and Aniwaniwa Tait-Jones.
Head coach JJ Redick said adding wings put Dalton Knecht on the roster bubble as LA trims to 15.
The Lakers must finalize their roster before opening the regular season against Golden State on Wednesday.
body: The Los Angeles Lakers are still trying to figure out how to trim their roster to 15 players, whether through a trade or by waiving someone. LA has made several moves this offseason to reach this point, but some roster decisions remain unresolved.

There are a few potential candidates, but Dalton Knecht has been widely viewed as the player most likely to be let go. Even before the preseason began, Knecht faced an uphill battle to secure his spot on the roster.

“My assumption is that if they had to make a decision right now, they would not pick up the $6.4 million team-option on Dalton Knecht. He's got between now and Halloween to change their mind," Lakers analyst Trevor Lane said.
Ahead of Friday night's preseason finale, Lakers head coach JJ Redick met with the media and explained why Knecht has found himself on the roster bubble.

“I think the biggest thing is the team changed. The team changed. Needs changed, the fit changed. I think he’s gotten better as a player the last two years. I think, particularly last year, each guy got plenty of opportunities with the injuries we had. I just think coming into this year, we added a lot of wings and he’s in a tough spot right now,” Redick said.
On Saturday, Los Angeles waived two players, neither of whom was Knecht.

“The Lakers have waived Rafael Castro and Aniwaniwa Tait-Jones, the team announced. LAL has a couple more training camp practices remaining before opening the regular season against GSW on Wednesday,” ESPN’s Dave McMenamin wrote.

Castro and Tait-Jones were not part of the 16-man roster, meaning Knecht remains on the chopping block and could still be waived. However, the Lakers' latest moves also suggest they are continuing to explore a potential trade to finalize their roster.
Time is running out for Los Angeles to make a final decision. With the regular season set to begin Wednesday, the Lakers will need to resolve Knecht's roster situation soon.

articles.headline: More than 1,800 arrested in France after protester violence erupts
keyFacts: Police arrested at least 1,800 people across France after violent clashes and looting erupted during nationwide protests over living costs.
Officials said between 550,000 and 800,000 people demonstrated, leaving more than 500 police officers and firefighters injured.
President Emmanuel Macron pledged that looters will pay for damages and those who targeted the Republic will be held accountable.
body: Police arrested at least 1,800 people across France after violent groups clashed with officers and looted shops during nationwide demonstrations that drew hundreds of thousands who denounced rising living costs and
Authorities said masked groups on Saturday set fires and attacked public buildings, including city halls, in several cities.

In Limoges, a city in central France, flames engulfed the 19th-century City Hall, causing its roof to collapse. Haute-Vienne prefect Maurice Barate told LCI television that the fire was deliberately set and nearly destroyed the building. The fire was under control Sunday.
French President Emmanuel Macron held an emergency meeting with top government officials on Sunday afternoon and later addressed the nation.
"Those who looted will have to pay back for the damage, and those who sought to bring down the Republic will be held accountable," Macron said.
He pointed to "unrestrained violence" by "insurrectionist elements from radical far-left groups, joined by numerous criminals."

"The right to protest is a fundamental right. Deliberately and collectively sowing disorder through violence is not," Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez wrote on X earlier, pointing to the looting of hundreds of businesses in many cities including Paris, Marseille, Lyon and Bordeaux.

About 550,000 people took part in protests across France, according to authorities, while organizers counted about 800,000. More than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters were injured, Nuñez said.
One person died of a heart attack, Paris police said in a statement, without providing details. Paris prosecutors' office said it was investigating.
"Stunned by the level of destruction"

Around Paris' Place de la République on Sunday morning, dislodged cobblestones, shattered storefronts and broken glass marked the aftermath of the events. Looting and damage were reported around the square and in some other tourist and shopping areas in the city center.
Paris police said Sunday that 855 people were arrested in the French capital region alone. The Paris prosecutors' office said that 557 of them were kept in police custody.
"I am actually stunned by the level of destruction and violence that was expressed," Marie Peyreigne, a 57-year-old government employee, said, wondering what led to the mayhem.
Inspecting the damage, many Parisians took photos of the partially dismantled base of the central monument at Place de la République — a statue of Marianne, a symbol of France.
Jean Foissy, 74, said he wanted to join the protest but found "a wall of riot police and fires everywhere," and went back home.
"I was very scared," he said. "I've been a Parisian since I was born, so when I got here, it almost made me want to cry because I find it so bad, it hurts me."
Margaux Eude, 26, said she supports the protest movement but "didn't think it would escalate like this."
"It's the troublemakers who came, and it breaks my heart because it delegitimizes the movement," she said.
Political leaders trade blame
Political leaders across the spectrum sought to parlay the fallout of Saturday's riots into political capital, looking ahead to next spring's presidential election.

Far-right leader and presidential hopeful Marine Le Pen lashed out at far-left rival Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who joined the Paris march. "Looting, ransacking, destroying and attacking law enforcement: Rioters have again spoiled the Oct. 17 demonstrations for the protection of purchasing power," Le Pen wrote on X.
Her running mate, Jordan Bardella, said on X that "if the silent majority of French decide it, we will reestablish order for the long term."

Mélenchon, for his part, traded barbs with the prime minister, accusing Lecornu of "playing with fire" and alleging that "by banking on degradation, you have only succeeded in uniting all youths and workers' unions."
Mélenchon insisted that "my message is clear: those who share our fight have no business in looting or destruction."
U.S. President Trump posted "France is burning!" on his Truth Social platform, apparently linking the unrest to "the immigration of people from an entirely different world."
"Close your Borders and take control, before it is too late!" he wrote.
French authorities and police have not linked immigrants to the rioting and have repeatedly attributed some of the violence to "radical far-left groups" and other people who joined to loot.

articles.headline: Eberechi Eze given harsh reality check over Arsenal future after ruthless Mikel Arteta act
keyFacts: Eberechi Eze was substituted at halftime during his first Premier League start of the season in Arsenal's 1-0 win over Nottingham Forest.
Former manager Alan Pardew said Eze may only serve as an impact substitute rather than a regular starter for Arsenal.
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said he substituted Eze to bring on fresh legs against Forest's deep defensive line.
body: Eberechi Eze has been told he may need to accept his role at Arsenal being an impact substitute after a nightmare cameo.
Eze was handed his first start of the Premier League season during the Gunners ‘ 1-0 win over Nottingham Forest on Sunday.
Eze was hooked at half time during Arsenal’s 1-0 win over Nottingham Forest after being handed his first league start of the season Getty
However, the England international was substituted at half time at the City Ground by Mikel Arteta in a brutal decision.
To make matters worse, his replacement, Noni Madueke , was the player to score the late winning goal for the visitors.
In his first half showing, Eze lost possession eight times and failed to complete a dribble while playing off the left wing.
He also misplaced four of his passes and really struggled to make an impact against the deep defensive line of Forest.
And after failing to prove why he deserves a starting place, concerns are rising as to whether he’ll ever have a key role.
Will Eze ever become an Arsenal starter?
Speaking on talkSPORT’s The Final Word, host Majestic said: “Apart from bodying Spurs last season , he hasn’t really set the world on fire for Arsenal.
“I can’t help but think that the way Arteta sets his team up, the freedom that Eze needs a player…he doesn’t seem like an Arteta player.”
That then prompted ex-Premier League boss Alan Pardew to admit he thinks Eze won’t ever be a starter in this Arsenal team.
“In the way he sets up his No.10, I don’t see Eze getting a lot of action there,” Pardew said.
“There’s a real defensive side to that No.10 position he likes that Martin Odegaard does and Eze doesn’t do.
Pardew doesn’t think Eze will ever be a starter for Arsenal and that his role may be coming on as a late substitute Getty
“I think Arteta doesn’t feel comfortable with that.”
He added: “In certain games, against lesser oppositon, Eze will be given that No.10 position.

“But I’ve seen him on that left side for Crystal Palace a few times and it’s just not him. He’s never going to go down the left hand side and whip crosses in, he wants to come and play centrally. He’s going to make the game too narrow and therefore you’ve not got enough width, so it’s a problem.
“Arteta took him off rightly, in my opinion, as it just wasn’t working.
“In the first instance though, perhaps he shouldn’t have started him there, and used him as an impact as a No.10. And I think that will be his role at Arsenal, if they need a goal.
“I don’t think Eze is going to a starter for Arsenal, I think he’s a sub and if they need a moment, then the manager can give him the last 10-15 minutes of games.”
Arteta admitted it was tough for Eze coming up against a deep defensive line, but remained positive on his star Getty
What has Arteta said on Eze?
Arteta may have taken Eze off at the break against Forest on Sunday, but he remained positive on the midfielder post-match.
The 28-year-old scored for Arsenal in the Champions League on Tuesday after starting on the left wing against Lille.
“Three days ago he scored a goal, he should have scored three and we were all happy,” Arteta told Sky Sports.
He then went on to admit that Eze couldn’t find space against Nottingham Forest’s deep block, so he had to try a new approach.

“This is football, one day it’s brilliant, the next day, especially with attacking players to play against a team that defends with 10 players in and around the box, the nine dropping almost at the edge, it’s extremely difficult to get in there and that’s it.
“But that’s why you need fresh legs, a different profile and try different things.”

articles.headline: Patriots lead Jets 17-3 at halftime
keyFacts: The Patriots led the Jets 17-3 at halftime after Drake Maye threw a touchdown pass to Pop Douglas.
New England will receive the ball to start the third quarter.
The Jets trailed by 14 points at halftime despite holding the ball nearly twice as long as the Patriots.
body: The Patriots were able to extend their lead over the Jets late in the first half at Gillette Stadium.

After forcing a punt with just over a minute left in the second quarter, the Patriots were able to move the ball inside the Jets' 9-yard-line on a pass to Pop Douglas that was combined with a roughing the passer call on Jets rookie linebacker David Bailey. A pair of incompletions left the Patriots with one last chance to get the ball into the end zone before halftime and they took advantage of it.
Drake Maye scrambled long enough to find Douglas for a touchdown that pushed the Patriots to a 17-3 lead. New England will also get the ball to start the third quarter.

Maye has not been sacked despite the Patriots losing a pair of offensive linemen to injury. Right tackle Morgan Moses is questionable to return with an ankle injury and left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker has the same designation due to a hamstring injury. Wide receiver Romeo Doubs is also questionable to return after hurting his shoulder while catching Maye's first touchdown of the day.

The Jets opened the game with a field goal and moved the ball into Patriots territory twice more, but saw both drives end with failed attempts to convert on fourth down. The first was a run out of the shotgun by Braelon Allen and the second was a Geno Smith sneak that came after another shotgun run was thwarted on third down.
That's why the Jets trail by 14 despite having the ball nearly twice as long as the Patriots through one half of play.

articles.headline: Arsenal win with one shot on target as Forest sink into bottom three
keyFacts: Substitute Noni Madueke scored an 80th-minute deflected shot, giving Arsenal a one-nil victory over Nottingham Forest with their only shot on target.
The result leaves Arsenal three points behind Premier League leaders Manchester City, while Nottingham Forest dropped into the relegation zone.
Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner stated that the defeat was frustrating because his side defended well but failed to score at home.

Nottingham Forest 0-1 Arsenal: Noni Madueke's late deflected strike wins it with Gunners' only shot on target

Report and free match highlights as Noni Madueke’s deflected winner earned Arsenal a hard-fought victory at Nottingham Forest; the Gunners stay within three points of Premier League leaders Manchester City, while Forest drop into the relegation zone

Arsenal's only shot on target proved enough to snatch victory at Nottingham Forest through Noni Madueke's deflected strike, keeping the champions within touching distance of Premier League leaders Manchester City and condemning Forest to the relegation zone.

After 80 frustrating minutes at the City Ground, substitute Madueke cut inside from the left and fired towards goal. His strike deflected off Jair Cunha, wrong-footed Matz Sels and found the net to settle a game in which Arsenal had struggled to turn possession into chances.

Arsenal had dominated the ball but registered no shots on target in the first half. Kai Havertz headed wide from a Declan Rice free-kick while Gabriel's set-piece effort was cleared almost off the line by Ousmane Diomande.

Forest made life difficult for Mikel Arteta's side, defending resolutely and threatening on the counter. However, despite their opportunities, it was the same old story for Oliver Glasner's side, who failed to find a breakthrough.

The result takes Arsenal to 18 points, three behind leaders Manchester City. For Forest, the frustration deepens. They drop into the relegation zone and are still waiting for their first home league goal of the season.
Analysis: Eze must prove his worth as Arsenal's main man after Madueke shines
Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:
Eberechi Eze has spent a year at Arsenal since leaving Crystal Palace, but questions remain over whether he is ready to become one of the club's leading figures as their ambitions continue to grow.
His talent is undeniable. The real concern is whether he can influence games consistently, and the trip to Nottingham Forest presented another opportunity to silence his doubters.

With Arsenal struggling to break down Forest, Eze had the chance to make a difference. Instead, he was substituted at half-time, watching from the sidelines as Noni Madueke replaced him and went on to score the 80th-minute winner.
Roy Keane's assessment on Sky Sports was telling, suggesting his concerns extended beyond a single performance.
"We're still waiting for him, the talent is there," Keane said. "We just want him to be at Arsenal and be able to take responsibility and try to be the main man at a big club."

That is the challenge facing Eze. At Crystal Palace, he was the focal point, the player expected to create chances and turn games in his team's favour. At Arsenal, however, talent alone will not earn him that status. He must deliver consistently, particularly in tight contests when his team need inspiration.
Ian Wright offered some important context, describing Eze as a "moments player" who benefits from having players around him and can become isolated on the left.
There is merit to that argument. Eze offers a different threat to Madueke, whose pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders gave Arsenal a fresh dimension in the second half.
Yet that only underlines the challenge facing the former Palace man. While Madueke seized his opportunity and made an immediate impact, Eze failed to leave his mark on the contest.

Competition for places is healthy at a club with Arsenal's ambitions. For Eze, though, the task is no longer simply to showcase his ability in flashes. He must demonstrate that he can influence games regularly, take responsibility when his team need him and establish himself as a first-choice player.
The talent is there. Now, Eze must prove he can turn that potential into consistent performances and become one of Arsenal's main men."
Forest's lack of goals has caught up with them
Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:
There was only so long Nottingham Forest could rely on defensive resilience before their lack of goals caught up with them. Now they are in the relegation zone.
Oliver Glasner's side have failed to score in every Premier League home game this season, and their defeat to Arsenal highlighted why they are in trouble.
Forest competed and created opportunities, but lacked the quality in the final third to make their efforts count.
Liam Delap struggled to make an impact against Arsenal's defence, summing up a frustrating afternoon. Forest needed someone to take responsibility, but their attacking play lacked conviction.
That is the worry for Glasner. Defensive organisation can only take a team so far; they still need goals to win matches.

Forest are now in the relegation zone with just five points. Their performances offer some encouragement, but until they find a reliable source of goals at the City Ground, it is difficult to see their situation improving."

Arteta: We knew margins would be small
Mikel Arteta to Sky Sports:
"We did something we didn't do in the two seasons before and that is win the game.

"The longer the game goes on, they have more belief and that's when you have to take more risks and that when the game can break.
"But we talked about it. We had to be so patient, without getting frustrated.
"It was tough to generate open chances against them. And we have to take them when we get them.
"We had another three chances [in the gme] that should have been on target.
"And not only on target, but they should have been goal.
"That's the difference, you have to be clinical."
Glasner: Have to take your chances against the champions
Oliver Glasner to Sky Sports:
"I think everybody feels the result is unfair today (in terms of the way we performed).
"But it's another defeat and another game when we couldn't score at the City Ground.
"But the performance today, especially defensively was of the top level.
"It was their only shot on target (that Arsenal scored from) and this one was deflected and Arsenal took the win.
"We also had our moments and it's important when you play the champions you take your moments.
"But today, the performance, effort, spirit and energy we had was on a very good level. But the result is frustrating."

articles.headline: A woman was arrested in Philly for blocking a delivery robot
keyFacts: Carolyn Marvin was arrested and charged with disorderly conduct after refusing police orders to stop blocking an Uber delivery robot.

body: Carolyn Marvin was arrested and charged with disorderly conduct after blocking the path of an Uber delivery robot and refusing to get out of the way. Marvin told Philadelphia’s ABC13 “I know they’re taking the jobs of human delivery workers and so, I have been protesting them whenever I saw them by standing in front of them and preventing them from going forward.”

Police responded to the scene and asked Marvin to move out of the robot’s way. When she refused, they placed her in cuffs and arrested her. The incident was captured on video and has now garnered considerable media attention.

The delivery robots have become a common sight on the streets of downtown Philadelphia and have sparked backlash. This is not even Marvin’s first brush with them. And earlier this year, one was kicked over in Center City. articles.headline: Falcons honor Jeff Ulbrich's late wife Cristina with emotional pregame tribute against Bears
keyFacts: Atlanta Falcons players wore warmup shirts honoring Cristina Ulbrich, the late wife of defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich, before their game against the Chicago Bears.
Cristina Ulbrich died in July at age 48 following a lengthy battle with cancer, leaving behind her husband and three children.
The pregame tribute demonstrated ongoing support from the Falcons organization and players for Jeff Ulbrich following his wife's passing.
body: The Atlanta Falcons took the field Sunday with more than football on their minds, delivering an emotional tribute to defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich and his late wife, Cristina Ulbrich, who died earlier this year following a lengthy battle with cancer.
Before Sunday's matchup against the Chicago Bears at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, Falcons players wore red warmup shirts featuring the message, "I Play for Cristina Ulbrich."
The tribute served as a reminder that the relationships within an NFL organization extend far beyond wins, losses and what happens on the football field.
Cristina died in July at age 48 after battling cancer. She leaves behind Jeff and their three children, Samantha, Jax and Jace.
Following her passing, the Falcons released a statement honoring her impact on the organization.
"Cristina was a devoted wife, mother, and friend whose strength, grace, and resilience touched all who knew her," the organization stated.
Falcons owner Arthur Blank also expressed his condolences, emphasizing Cristina's importance to the organization.
"Cristina will always be an important part of our Falcons family," Blank said.
Falcons continue supporting Jeff Ulbrich through difficult time
Ulbrich stepped away from the team during training camp to spend time with his family following Cristina's passing.
His return brought emotional support from players who viewed their defensive coordinator as more than a football coach.
Falcons linebacker Divine Deablo previously described Ulbrich as a father figure and older brother, emphasizing the respect players have for their coach.
Sunday's tribute demonstrated that the bond remains strong.
For Atlanta, the message represented something bigger than a Week 6 matchup against Chicago.
It was an opportunity to recognize Cristina's courage, honor her memory and remind Ulbrich that his football family continues standing beside him.
While the Falcons entered Sunday looking for an important victory, the pregame tribute carried a deeper meaning.
Football brings players and coaches together, but moments like these demonstrate the compassion and unity that can develop within a locker room.
Regardless of Sunday's outcome, the Falcons delivered a powerful message through their red shirts: Cristina Ulbrich's memory remains part of the organization.

keyFacts: Massachusetts Republican lieutenant governor candidate Shawn Oliver was arrested for operating under the influence after a crash, police said.
Police stated Oliver's vehicle struck five parked cars and overturned in New Bedford, leading to multiple driving charges.
Gubernatorial running mate Mike Minogue called on Oliver to immediately suspend his campaign following the arrest.
body: Massachusetts Republican candidate for lieutenant governor Shawn Oliver was arrested and charged with operating under the influence of alcohol Saturday night, police said.

Around 11:40 p.m., the New Bedford Police Department responded to reports at 448 Dartmouth St. that a vehicle was overturned after striking multiple parked vehicles. Five parked vehicles were struck, with two sustaining “extensive damage,” police spokeswoman Holly Huntoon told the Washington Examiner .

Oliver, who also serves as a New Bedford city councilman, was taken to St. Luke’s Hospital for treatment. After an investigation, Oliver was arrested and charged with operating under the influence of liquor, negligent operation of a motor vehicle, a marked lanes violation, and speeding, according to police.
The 42-year-old’s running mate, Republican gubernatorial candidate Mike Minogue, posted a statement on social media on Sunday, calling for Oliver’s resignation.

“I am extremely disappointed,” Minogue wrote on X . “Shawn is lucky to be alive and lucky that no one innocent was hurt. There is no excuse for driving under the influence. After speaking with Shawn, I am asking him to suspend his campaign immediately, and when elected, I will formally ask for his resignation. Shawn is a father and grandfather, and he needs to put his family first. He needs to do the work to ensure this never happens again. If he needs help with that, I will help him. As governor, I will put the Commonwealth first. That starts with accountability, something Massachusetts has not seen from Maura Healey.”
New Bedford Mayor Jon Mitchell also released a statement, calling the incident “concerning.”
MASSACHUSETTS STARTER-HOME BALLOT MEASURE TESTS TAKING HOUSING SUPPLY DIRECTLY TO VOTERS

“This morning, I was made aware that City Councilor Shawn Oliver was involved in a car accident in the South End and taken into custody,” Mitchell wrote on Facebook . “I’m grateful to the New Bedford Police Department for their prompt response and relieved that no one was seriously injured. The allegations against Councilor Oliver are deeply concerning, and the public deserves to hear his explanation of what happened.”
The Washington Examiner reached out to Oliver’s office for comment.

articles.headline: Northampton beat Cardiff for only English win of Champions Cup openers
keyFacts: Northampton defeated Cardiff 28-12 at Franklin's Gardens to become the only English team to win in the opening round of the Champions Cup.

Northampton became the only English side to win in the opening round of the Champions Cup by battling past Cardiff.
Saints, quarter-finalists last season, scored four tries at Franklin's Gardens in a nervy Pool Four encounter.
The English champions led 14-0 at half-time thanks to efforts in tricky conditions by James Pater and Toby Thame.
Tenacious Cardiff struck back through Harri Millard and Mason Grady to make it a two-point game in the final quarter.
But George Hendy and Fraser Dingwall responded as Northampton got off to a winning start, albeit without a bonus point.
Northampton's success came at the end of a chastening opening weekend of the top-tier tournament for Prem clubs, with Gloucester drawing against champions Bordeaux-Begles but six other sides losing.
Cardiff's return to the top tier of Europe after two seasons in the Challenge Cup was a considerable one.
Saints had scored 24 tries in their three opening fixtures of their Prem title defence, including 11 against Bath last time out at Franklin's Gardens.
The Welsh side also had to contend with a five-day turnaround to a United Rugby Championship (URC) fixture against Sharks at Cardiff Arms Park.
That led to several influential players being held back, although they did give first appearances of the season to Wales and Lions internationals Taulupe Faletau and Josh Adams after injury.
Northampton also made changes because of a big fixture on the horizon - the short trip to Leicester on Saturday - but got the job done.
Full-back Pater opened the scoring for Saints with a supporting run and centre Thame crashed over after 20 minutes.
Both Northampton number eight Callum Chick and Cardiff lock Tom Manz knocked on going for the line as slippery conditions led to it being 14-0 at half-time.
The Blue and Blacks struck back early in the second half when centre Millard hit a nice line in the 22 and then defended stoutly to frustrate their hosts, forcing them into a raft of handling errors.
It was 14-12 on the hour when, after Saints fly-half Anthony Belleau was sin-binned for a breakdown offence, the ball was floated to the right by Jarrod Evans for Grady to cross.
Cardiff scented an upset only for Hendy to respond swiftly, juggling the ball for a try that Pater converted.
The Northampton wing went from scoring five points to saving them by chasing down Adams when a try seemed certain.
Dingwall dashed over in the 78th minute but the hosts could not find the fifth try that was needed for a five-point haul.
Saints travel to Stade Francais in December and return to France in January to face Montpellier before a home finish to the group stage against Bulls.

articles.headline: 36 Years Later, Robert De Niro's Greatest Gangster Movie Quote Is Still One of a Kind
keyFacts: In Martin Scorsese's Goodfellas, Robert De Niro's character James Conway tells young Henry Hill to never rat on friends and keep his mouth shut.
Polygon reports that this simple line of advice outlines the strict code of loyalty and silence required to survive in the criminal underworld.
The article notes that the quote remains memorable 36 years later because the gangsters' loyalty ultimately collapses under the weight of greed and self-preservation.
body: Few actors have done more to shape the modern cinematic gangster than Robert De Niro. Across decades of mob dramas, he's played men who command respect through intimidation, calculation, and a religious devotion to the rules of their world. From The Godfather to The Irishman, De Niro's proven himself one of the most popular leading men to handle some of the worst gangsters on the silver screen, including Al Capone, Vito Corleone, Frank Costello, David “Noodles” Aaronson, James Burke, and plenty more.

Through all these roles, De Niro has delivered plenty of unforgettable lines, but one of his most memorable isn't a threat or a declaration of power. It's a deceptively simple piece of advice, one that succinctly sums up the gangster mentality built on loyalty. Ripped from Martin Scorsese's Goodfellas (based on Nicholas Pilegg's non-fiction crime chronicle Wiseguy), De Niro’s James “Jimmy” Conway offers the following sage advice: "Never rat on your friends and always keep your mouth shut."

The line comes after a young Henry Hill (Ray Liotta) refuses to talk following a bust for selling untaxed cigarettes, earning his stripes by making it through his first court appearance without informing on any of his accomplices. Outside the courtroom, Conway slips him a handful of cash and congratulates him on surviving his first pinch. Then he pulls Henry close and imparts the cardinal rules of their world, turning a low-level arrest into a defining rite of passage for a kid desperate to prove his place in the organization.

Delivered with De Niro's characteristic matter-of-fact calm, the line feels less like friendly advice and more like a warning about what happens to anyone who breaks the code. It's one of the most revealing glimpses into the criminal underworld these characters occupy and rule over. For all the money, violence, and excess that define the lives of Hill, Conway, Tommy DeVito (Joe Pesci) and their associates, survival depends on an unspoken code. You don't betray your fellow gangsters, and you certainly don't cooperate with the authorities. Break those rules, and you're no longer one of them.
The cruel irony of mob life

What's fascinating about this Goodfellas quote is how reasonable it can sound at first. Loyalty and discretion are admirable qualities in most walks of life, after all, but the events of Goodfellas strip those virtues of their romantic associations, revealing how easily they can twist into instruments of control when followed by professional criminals. Jimmy isn't offering Henry a heartfelt lesson about friendship. He's explaining the conditions under which men like them are allowed to operate. In their world, keeping loyal and keeping quiet are a matter of life and death.

Henry's journey in Goodfellas is defined by a violent push-and-pull between the seductive illusion of mob privilege and its lethal reality. On one hand, he revels in the effortless power of the gangster lifestyle, famously walking his future-wife Karen (Lorraine Bracco) straight past the Copacabana kitchen to a personal table like royalty. On the other hand, he exists within a paranoid vacuum where those "friends" are inherently dangerous. The same men who provide him with cash, status, and immunity are also capable of turning on anyone they perceive as a threat, as Conway demonstrates when he begins eliminating his own associates after the Lufthansa heist. His easygoing demeanor masks a ruthless instinct for self-preservation, and Henry's proximity to that violence makes it increasingly clear that the loyalty holding their world together only lasts as long as it's convenient.

De Niro's performance also makes the quote particularly effective. Jimmy Conway isn't the loudest or most outwardly volatile gangster in the film. He's often charming, even generous, and De Niro understands that a man capable of terrible violence doesn't need to announce himself as dangerous. Jimmy's advice carries weight because the audience has already seen the ruthlessness lurking beneath his affable exterior. The movie’s opening scene is enough to introduce us to the bloodbath that’s set to follow. When Conway talks about loyalty, there's an implicit warning that makes the sentiment considerably less comforting.

The tragedy is that the code Conway describes is never quite as dependable as the gangsters want to believe. Their loyalty lasts only as long as it remains convenient, and their friendships are threatened by their own greed, ambition, and the constant possibility of incarceration. As Henry's circumstances deteriorate, the promise of lifelong allegiance gives way to the practical business of staying alive. The very rules that once made him feel protected become impossible to follow if he wants to truly survive.

Conway’s line endures because it captures the central contradiction at the heart of Goodfellas. These men depend on loyalty because they cannot trust anyone outside their circle, yet the lives they've chosen make genuine trust unattainable. Jimmy’s doctrine might serve as gospel within the criminal underworld, but it offers zero salvation in a meat-grinder where silence only buys time and a best friend's nod is just a prelude to a bullet in the back of the head.
Goodfellas is streaming on Howdy.

articles.headline: The Lindsay Clancy case exposes the insanity defense loophole
keyFacts: Lindsay Clancy's murder trial ended in a mistrial after eleven of twelve jurors supported her insanity defense.
Defense attorney Kevin Reddington subsequently asked a judge to dismiss the case, claiming insufficient evidence proved Clancy killed her children.
The author noted that prosecutors may try Clancy again, while arguing that legal insanity defenses function as loopholes that undermine justice.
body: The insanity defense and incompetency rulings are being rampantly abused by defense attorneys and soft-on- crime judges, making a mockery of the criminal justice system and the victims of crime in the process.

The case of Lindsay Clancy brought a renewed focus on this issue. Clancy murdered her three children by strangulation and pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity, claiming postpartum psychosis. The claim itself is dubious, given that Clancy deliberately strangled each of her three children to death over a span of several minutes after deliberately sending and keeping her husband out of the house on errands. Clancy claimed to have killed her children because she heard a voice tell her to do so, and yet has not claimed to hear that voice before or since despite her alleged history of mental turmoil.
LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR DISCUSSES HARASSMENT, FEARS, AND MEDIA ATTENTION AFTER MISTRIAL

Throughout the trial, Clancy and her legal team acknowledged that she killed her children but maintained that she should not be held criminally responsible, hence the decision to plead not guilty due to insanity. Her lawyer, Kevin Reddington, repeatedly acknowledged that Clancy killed her children, claiming that it was a cocktail of medications and untreated psychosis that were responsible. The insanity defense was full of holes, but the one undeniable fact that everyone agreed on was that Lindsay Clancy killed her children.
The defense almost worked. The jury deadlocked, and the trial was ruled a mistrial, but 11 of the 12 jurors supported Clancy’s insanity defense.
Only later came the proof that Clancy and her team were abusing the insanity defense.

After Reddington failed to remove the holdout juror (and launched a legal and media pressure campaign to intimidate potential future jurors), he decided that Clancy did not kill her children at all. Reddington instead asked the judge to throw out the case entirely because “There is not enough evidence that this woman killed those children” and “this entire case is based on speculation.” Emboldened by the near victory with the jury, Reddington abandoned the central tenet of the insanity defense — that Clancy killed her children — and the insanity plea along with it.

In other words, Reddington essentially admitted to lying to the jury and the public to get the verdict he wanted for his client. The insanity plea was just a tool, one that he used to free Clancy and one that he will almost certainly return to if prosecutors decide to try the case again.
This is not a defense attorney merely advocating for his client; it is a defense attorney manipulating the system and undermining trust in jury trials, one insincere insanity plea at a time.

The common refrain you may hear in response to much of this is that being found not guilty by insanity does not allow a criminal to “go free,” but that is essentially what it does. In Massachusetts , if Clancy had been found not guilty by insanity, she would undergo up to 40 days of evaluations before potentially being committed for a period of six months. A judge would then review her status every year, meaning she could realistically only serve a few years in an institution before walking free. Or a mere six months.

A prime example comes from Kentucky . In 2015, Ronald Exantus broke into a home and stabbed a 6-year-old boy to death. Exantus was found not guilty by reason of insanity for that murder and guilty but mentally ill on three counts of attacking the boy’s family members. He served a grand total of seven years in prison, and was not subject to an immediate involuntary hospitalization proceeding after being released.

In other words, Exantus stabbed a child to death, pleaded insanity, and walked free within seven years. He was deemed so insane that he could snap and brutally murder a child at a moment’s notice, and yet he was loosed on the public.

Others don’t even need to wait seven years, thanks to the incompetence loophole. Whereas criminals found not guilty by insanity can avoid true justice for their crimes, alleged criminals deemed incompetent to stand trial can avoid even going through the trial process at all. Take DeCarlos Brown Jr., the man accused of brutally stabbing Ukrainian refugee Iryna Zarutska to death on a North Carolina train in an infamous 2025 case.

Brown had a long criminal history prior to the incident, but he was free to roam the streets because his most recent trial had been delayed. Brown’s defense attorney had requested a mental health evaluation, and the judge simply released Brown to pursue that evaluation on his own time. Unsurprisingly, he never did. It cost Iryna Zarutska her life.

The incompetency sham continued, with Brown being declared incompetent to stand trial in the murder case. Supposedly, Brown is not mentally competent enough to contribute to his own defense, but was mentally competent enough to flee the scene after the murder and attempt to discard both the alleged murder weapon (the knife) and the sweatshirt he was wearing that could be used to identify him by appearance. And, like seemingly all violent criminals deemed “insane” or “incompetent” in random acts of public violence, Brown just so happened to allegedly target a small, vulnerable woman incapable of fighting back.

Take a more recent example in Rhode Island , where Nelson Blanco was walking free despite a 30-year history of crime. Blanco allegedly stabbed two children in 2003 but was deemed unfit to stand trial, was deemed incompetent to stand trial in 2018 for being in possession of a stolen vehicle, and was arrested for domestic violence in 2024. However, in 2025, he was released to the custody of Rhode Island health officials. That led to him being back out on the street a year later, where he allegedly stabbed a mother and her child (again, two vulnerable victims incapable of fighting back) earlier this month. The two-year-old girl is still in critical condition.
CALIFORNIA: WHERE ATTEMPTED MURDER IS WORTH ONE DAY IN JAIL

In all of the cases listed above (not counting Clancy), these men were deemed too crazy to understand whether their acts were right or wrong or the fact that they were on trial. And yet, based on the incompetency and insanity laws that are on the books, they were protected from facing justice for their crimes and not institutionalized for the rest of their lives. Too crazy to face the justice system, but not crazy enough to prevent them from walking the streets alongside the women and children that they (allegedly) went on to victimize.

As the Clancy case has shown, these insanity and incompetency rulings are increasingly insincere, a tactic taken up by criminals and their defense attorneys, knowing the law treats “insane” criminals with kid gloves. The insanity defense and incompetent to stand trial rulings do nothing to benefit the public or the few criminals who are genuinely insane, who are released instead of receiving the long-term institutional care they need. They serve now only as a loophole for criminals who hope that the justice system will excuse them from their crimes on mental health grounds.

articles.headline: From the Royole FlexPai to the iPhone Duo: How the modern foldable phone has evolved
keyFacts: Apple entered the foldable smartphone market by announcing the iPhone Duo in 2026 with a starting price of $1,999.
Early foldables suffered design issues before Android manufacturers spent years improving durability, water resistance, and crease visibility.
Counterpoint told Bloomberg that sales of the iPhone Duo are expected to reach six million units in 2026.
body: From the Royole FlexPai to the iPhone Duo: How the modern foldable phone has evolved
Are foldables finally ready to go mainstream?

Technological advances often come with growing pains. This is no less true of phones. The 1984 "brick" phone (DynaTAC 8000X) required users to carry over 1.7 pounds of weight for only half an hour of talk time, at a hefty price tag of $3,995. Foldable phones are not so troublesome, but I still struggled to fit the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 4 in my pocket when I first got it. What's more, the size of it kept prompting friends to ask why I was carrying two phones around. I wish I had been, for at least it would mean one would have a decent camera. Still, the moment when the phone unfolded and the screen adjusted to the larger size was as awe-inspiring back then as it is now.

Today, after having gotten my hands on some newer models, I have become very impressed by the lengths foldable technology has reached. Models including the Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold and the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 have propelled the technology forward. Even Apple has decided to enter the market, with the iPhone Duo launch that has everyone talking. Suddenly, the future uptake of foldable phones is almost a certainty. Apple might well end up having everything to do with this change, but it would not have been possible without the long list of breakthroughs — and failures — that came before it.
The first stumbles: Royole, Samsung and Huawei

Trend pieces declared 2019 the "year of the foldable." It was not, though those 12 months did provide the first meaningful strides in the technology. The first device of this type to make a splash in the headlines was designed by an unknown Chinese display manufacturer: Royole. The company presented the FlexPai at CES 2019, with all the pomp and circumstance that "the world's first commercially available foldable smartphone" required. It was a feat of technology. It captivated the audience, if only momentarily. For all its charms, Engadget's reporters at the time found the Royole FlexPai to be "rough around the edges," strangely sized and, overall, "janky." Regardless, it demonstrated that flexible OLED could ship in a real product.

Later that year came a second attempt. Samsung's first Galaxy Fold was released in February 2019, kick-starting a series of unfortunate events for the phone manufacturer. If you were there, you might remember the influx of terrible reviews that followed. Despite a high price (just under $2,000), many reviewers complained that their phone screens had broken after little use, and it was revealed that most of them had peeled off a layer of plastic that was acting as a screen protector. The phone's fragility forced Samsung to delay the public launch and recall all units sent to reviewers so it could re-engineer the product. The new version was, however, only "somewhat" more sturdy. Overall, those first Samsung phones showed the importance of perfecting the crease, hinge durability and screen resistance as key to the success of foldable phones.

The next step showed the route not taken. Huawei's Mate X, presented at MWC 2019, folded outward instead of inward. It used a single high-resolution display that wrapped around the outside of the phone. The resulting design was extremely elegant. The problem? The screen could easily be scratched and damaged. On top of that, the phone was never sold in the United States due to the sanctions imposed by then-President Donald Trump on Chinese technologies. Still, for as striking as the Mate X was, the company's next foldable, the Mate X2, used the inward fold introduced by Royole and Samsung, showing that different does not necessarily mean better.
The Android maturity years

The years between 2020 and 2025 gave way to an avalanche of foldable phone models, pushed by Android phone makers. Almost every phone released over these years came with a significant advance. It was all this hard work that has made the foldable phone viable. Still, no specific model achieved what the manufacturers truly wanted: to make the foldable phone mainstream.

At first, foldable phone makers were mainly concerned with protecting the screens against pressure, water and dust. In 2020, Samsung's Galaxy Z Flip introduced ultra-thin glass in the inner screen, making it more robust. The Z Fold 3 and Z Flip 3, released in 2021, came with IPX8 water resistance. Dust was harder to protect against than water, but still the Fold 6 came with partial dust protection (IP48). In 2025, Google's Pixel 10 Pro Fold reached full IP68. The other big battle was how to address the crease. It was Oppo, with its 2021 Find N, that achieved a near-invisible crease. After that, Honor's Magic V series kept cutting thickness until Samsung answered with the slim Galaxy Z Fold 7.

The other element that needed to change for the technology to be widespread was pricing. Over this period, clamshell phones like the rebooted Motorola Razr and the $999 Galaxy Z Flip 3 brought prices down to regular flagship levels, making foldable phones better for everyone's physical and figurative pockets.
Apple comes to town
Can Apple make the final push that will take foldable phones into the mainstream? It has done it before and could, no doubt, do it again if the iPhone Duo is everything that has been promised.

During its history, Apple has mastered the ability to wait until the first hiccups of a technology have passed before entering a market and disrupting it. The company did it with touchscreens, and again with foldable phones, waiting until the crease problem that Samsung struggled with had been resolved before putting out its own model. In 2026, the announcement finally arrived in the form of the iPhone Duo. Folded, the phone is passport-sized. It has a 7.6-inch internal display and a 5.4-inch external display, at a starting price of $1,999. Overall, it has all the ingredients to be a huge success, with reviewers deeming the iPhone Duo Apple's "most exciting device in a decade." Counterpoint even told Bloomberg the phone's sales are expected to reach 6 million units in 2026 alone. Taking Apple's history as a guide, we could be about to witness the exact moment when foldable phones finally become fashionable.

articles.headline: Photos show aftermath of riots as masked groups clash with police across France
keyFacts: Police reported 1,800 arrests across France after violent clashes, looting, and fires erupted during nationwide demonstrations over living costs and school conditions.

French media reported President Emmanuel Macron attended a concert during the unrest, while Donald Trump blamed immigration for the violence.
body: Paris woke Sunday to shattered storefronts, burned cars and a heavy police presence after unrest swept through the city and other parts of France.

Violent clashes broke out Saturday during nationwide demonstrations over rising living costs and poor school conditions. Hundreds of thousands marched across the country, while masked groups fought with police, looted businesses and set fires in several cities.
Police reported 1,800 arrests nationwide, including 855 in the Paris region.
VIOLENCE ERUPTS AT FRANCE PROTESTS AS MACRON WARNS UNREST IS BEING EXPLOITED
The destruction was not limited to Paris.
In Limoges, about three hours south of the capital, fire tore through the city’s historic town hall, built in 1883 and designated a historic landmark in 1975.

The local prefect, Maurice Barate, told AFP that the roof had collapsed onto the lower floors and about two-thirds of the building’s exterior had disappeared. He called it "a catastrophe for heritage."
LIMOGES TOWN HALL ‘LARGELY LOST’ AFTER FAR-LEFT RIOTERS SET HISTORIC BUILDING ON FIRE
French President Emmanuel Macron had called for "calm and respect" ahead of Saturday’s demonstrations, saying the right to protest must be exercised with respect for people and property.
But as violence escalated, the French president and his wife, Brigitte, were spotted at a Celine Dion concert in Nanterre, west of Paris, according to French media reports.
The couple reportedly arrived and left discreetly and joined roughly 35,000 spectators at the Plenitude Arena. Macron had spent Thursday and Friday in Brussels for a European Council meeting.
WHERE'S MACRON? FRENCH LEADER BLASTED FOR ATTENDING CONCERT AS RIOTS ESCALATED
President Donald Trump weighed in Sunday, blaming immigration for the unrest in a Truth Social post and urging France to close its borders.

"The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country," he wrote. "Close your borders and take control, before it is too late!"

articles.headline: Battlefield 6 devs to fix "Secuty" skin typo, but five-pistol outfit was intentional
keyFacts: Battlefield Studios announced that a typo reading 'Secuty' on a Battlefield 6 Season 5 skin will be fixed in an upcoming correction update.
The studio stated that a separate skin featuring five pistols was an intentional creative concept inspired by action movie tropes.
Battlefield Studios did not address fan accusations that generative AI was used to create the cosmetics.
body: Battlefield Studios has responded after fans accused it of using AI to generate cosmetics after spotting a "Secuty" typo on a Battlefield 6 Season 5 skin.
The studio acknowledged "candid feedback" from players in a statement on social media, insisting it had "hear[d] your concerns".

And though the statement did not mention AI - either to admit or deny using the generative tech - BattlefieldComm said that while the 'Secuty' typo will be addressed by a "correction update", an outfit with five pistols is intentional.

"First, let's dive into the 'Secuty' typo patches on the McNeil character," the studio wrote. "A correction update has already been planned for the Season 5 Phase 2 release. However, we recognise that letting a known visual error go live without quick acknowledgement creates confusion and erodes trust. We are reviewing how we communicate known visual bugs so you aren’t left wondering whether something was intentional or overlooked."

The five-pistol-touting Midnight Mirage skin, however, is described as an "intentional creative concept" and "a nod to over-the-top action movie tropes where an operative inexplicably has another backup weapon strapped to every spare inch of gear".

"That said, we understand how this could look unintentional when released alongside other cosmetic anomalies," the team added, and, specifically addressing the typo, said: "We take pride in the craft of our world and our gear, and seeing visual oddities slip through is frustrating for everyone."
Cosmetic Quality & Recent Feedback
Over the past week, we’ve seen conversation, memes, and candid feedback around a few of our latest skins and cosmetic items—specifically the standard issue McNeil skin with “SECUTY” typo.
You called it out clearly, and we hear your concerns.…
— Battlefield Comms (@BattlefieldComm) October 16, 2026
The message did not say how the typo happened or address fan accusations that generative AI was used.

Season 5 launched in Battlefield 6 this week as planned, and though most of the new additions - new maps, weapons and vehicles, and gameplay changes - were well received, the season began on a low note due to those aforementioned accusations of generative AI use and a major hit to XP gain.

articles.headline: Vance reveals ‘there’s a chance’ he won’t run for president in 2028: ‘We’ve got 4 little kids’
keyFacts: Vice President JD Vance said there is a chance he will not run for president in 2028, citing his family and four kids.

body: Vice President JD Vance revealed “there’s a chance” he won’t run for president in 2028 — and second lady Usha and the couple’s four young kids could help make the decision for him.
“We’ve got four little kids, my wife has never loved politics. She loves public service,” Vance said.
“I think you know you can do a lot of good in this job, and I’ve tried to do as much good as possible.”
The vice president said he has yet to make up his mind about a potential White House bid, describing himself as a “procrastinator” when it comes to major life decisions.
“The way that I think about life, big life decisions — my wife will tell you this: I’m a procrastinator. I hate thinking about it,” Vance said.

Vance indicated that he plans to give the question more serious consideration after the November midterm elections, rather than commit to a campaign while the Trump administration is still navigating its current agenda.
His comments come as the vice president is widely viewed as an early frontrunner to succeed Trump, who has described Vance as his “most likely” Republican successor.

The RealClear Polling average gives him a 15-point advantage over Secretary of State Marco Rubio in the Republican primary, with 39% support more than two years out from the 2028 election. President Trump’s son, Donald Jr., is third with 11% support.
In a March interview with NBC News, Usha said she sometimes holds views that do not fit neatly within traditional political camps.
“Sometimes I have thoughts that fit very comfortably into one side or another,” she said. “Sometimes I have views that are way more idiosyncratic.”
She also made clear that she sees herself as a sounding board for her husband rather than a political operative.
“I’m not his staffer. I’m not involved in this in any professional sense,” Usha said, adding that there is “no exception that we are going to see eye to eye on everything.”
Usha said in March that a 2028 presidential campaign was not yet a priority in their household, explaining that her husband was focused on the midterm elections and the demands of his current job.
“If you come back in 2027 and ask me, I’ll have a better sense of, you know, what he’s thinking in that way,” she told NBC News.
For now, Vance’s political future remains an open question — even as early polling puts him ahead of potential Republican rivals.

articles.headline: The Outlast Trials' initial playtests went poorly: Designer says 6-year development took 'a f**king long time' and 'a s**t-ton of prototypes'
keyFacts: Red Barrels co-founder Philippe Morin told Gamespot that developing The Outlast Trials took six years and numerous prototypes.
Morin said initial playtests of a build created within four years went poorly, forcing the team to redesign the game.
Morin stated the team initially went too far trying to make the game systemic and randomly generated for infinite replayability.
body: Gamedev may as well be conducted in a black box as far as many players are concerned, so it can be easy to think of a good game as one where development went smoothly and a bad game as one where things went terribly awry. But in the case of The Outlast Trials, making something sickeningly good took a lot of struggle.

As Red Barrels co-founder Philippe Morin told Gamespot in a recent interview, it took six years to turn the vague notion of a co-op Outlast game into something ready to launch via early access. It was "a fucking long time," as he recalled it, and the product of "a shit-ton of prototypes."

"[The Red Barrels team] went too far trying to make [The Outlast Trials] systemic, random, and trying to reach our ultimate goal of infinite replayability," he told Gamespot. "We needed to come back to something that maybe added less replayability, but definitely felt more like Outlast." The article notes that a seemingly shippable build was produced within four years, but playtests went poorly enough to send the team back to the drawing board.

I suppose concerns about replayability have been put to rest now that it's mutated into a sizable live service game with around 20,000 people playing as I write this, though the game's ongoing development isn't entirely free from strife—as the article points out, players are mixed on its use of AI-generated imagery, and Outlast 3 was seemingly put on the backburner after Trials proved a huge success.

articles.headline: How Trump’s justice department is shattering practice of political neutrality as midterms loom
keyFacts: Federal agents raided Representative Ilhan Omar's home and the Justice Department sued California over voter rolls ahead of the midterms.
Watchdogs claimed the department is interfering in elections, while an official said no policy bars actions close to an election.
The Justice Department asked a court to block California from counting ballots from 20,000 people with unconfirmed citizenship.
body: Donald Trump’s justice department has aggressively inserted itself into the midterm elections in the contest’s final weeks, shattering the department’s longstanding practice of political neutrality and leaving little doubt about the department’s willingness to help should the president attempt to subvert elections where his party is forecasted to lose seats and ultimately control of Congress.

In the last few weeks, federal agents have raided the home of a Democratic congresswoman up for re-election. It has touted criminal charges and arrests of non-citizens charged with voter fraud. The attorney general has hit the campaign trail to stump for Republican candidates. And the department gave California election officials 48 hours to investigate the citizenship of 20,000 people, and then sued the state when it refused to comply. The FBI also recently published a video criticizing Michigan senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and other Democrats, drawing an immediate rebuke from one watchdog, who said the video “has no place in a democratic society”.

On Monday, federal agents raided the DC home of Minnesota representative Ilhan Omar, who is running for re-election this fall. The raid was part of a reported immigration fraud investigation into Omar, an outspoken critic of the president, and an apparent push to try to denaturalize her. Omar is up for re-election, and Minnesota Democrats broadly are facing more headwinds than fellow party members in most other states.

“For decades, the justice department sought to avoid investigative steps that might influence an election, recognizing that election integrity is threatened when DoJ is perceived as putting its thumb on the scale,” said Stacey Young, a former justice department attorney who now leads Justice Connection, a group that supports justice department alumni.

“This was always a case-by-case analysis, led by experts in the public integrity section. But this administration pushed those experts out of the department, and employees seeking guidance are now directed to political appointees loyal to the president,” she added.

A justice department official said there is no rule or policy that bars the DoJ from taking action close to an election. The department is not required to stop ongoing work during election season, the official said.

A provision of the justice department manual says prosecutors and law enforcement agents should not take “any action, including investigative steps, criminal charges, or statements, for the purpose of affecting any election, or for the purpose of giving an advantage or disadvantage to any candidate or political party”. A separate provision of the manual says that “the Department should not engage in overt criminal investigative measures in matters involving alleged ballot fraud until the election in question has been concluded, its results certified, and all recounts and election contests concluded”.

An unwritten department practice has established a blackout window of at least 60 days before an election in which prosecutors should refrain from any activities that could influence the election. In September 2024, Todd Blanche, then serving as the president’s personal attorney, pointed to the rule to argue that special counsel Jack Smith should not be allowed to file a long brief with damaging information in the criminal election interference case against Trump. “Departures from these practices should never be countenanced because they risk allowing prosecutors to impact national elections,” Blanche wrote at the time. Experts disagreed with that argument at the time, pointing out that Smith was responding to a court-ordered deadline.

“For decades, the justice department has avoided even the appearance of political interference in the run-up to an election, and that’s exactly what the 60-day rule exists to protect,” said Skye Perryman, president and CEO of Democracy Forward, a watchdog group. “This DoJ is doing the opposite.”
Now, Blanche leads the justice department, and the 60-day rule seems to have gone out the window. The DoJ official said the 60-day rule was an informal practice.

Over the last few weeks, the department has sent out press releases announcing voter fraud charges against noncitizens with photos of their arrests. Noncitizen voting is extremely rare, and when it does occur, it is often because someone is confused about their eligibility. Court documents filed in many of the cases the justice department have charged contain little detail about whether the people charged knew they were ineligible.

“The DoJ’s actions ahead of the election, which violate longstanding norms, are extremely concerning. They are emblematic of how the Trump administration has repeatedly and illegally weaponized the federal law enforcement apparatus to interfere in our elections,” said Donald Sherman, president and CEO of Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (Crew), a watchdog group.
The department has also made a last-minute push to try to force states to purge voters from the rolls.

In an extraordinary move last week, the justice department sent election officials in Los Angeles a USB-drive with a handwritten password. The drive contained the names of potential noncitizens on the county’s rolls, the justice department said. The department gave county officials 48 hours to investigate the citizenship statuses and segregate ballots from anyone whose status they could not confirm and said the department would seek “emergency relief” if they did not.

Dean Logan, the top election official in Los Angeles, told the justice department his office would not be accessing the drive because it didn’t consider it secure. The department also didn’t say how many people were on the list and hadn’t described its methodology for identifying the voters. The department later said in a court filing it had provided the names of 20,000 people to the state.

After California rebuffed the DoJ’s efforts, the department sued the state on Thursday, requesting a court order blocking the state from counting the ballots from anyone among the 20,000 whose citizenship had not been confirmed.

The DoJ could have easily provided California with the names of people it suspected were on its voter rolls and its methodology for identifying them months ago, said David Becker, the executive director of the Center for Election Innovation and Research, a group that works on election administration issues. Instead, the department waited until after California had sent out mail-in ballots. Federal law also prohibits election officials from systematically purging voters within 90 days of a federal election.

“If they were seeking to work in good faith to clean up the voter list that they believed had issues, they would have done this months ago in a much different fashion,” Becker said. “However, it does raise questions as to whether or not the sole purpose of this is to set the stage for false claims about election theft after an election that the president might be worried his party was going to do poorly.”

In what may be the department’s most overtly political act, Blanche has also spoken at campaign rallies for Republican candidates and at the Republican convention in Dallas earlier this year. The department recently revised ethics guidance for officials appointed by the president and confirmed by the Senate to allow them to participate in more partisan political activities, according to a memo obtained by the PBS News Hour.
Blanche’s appearance raised concerns among ethics officials, despite the department’s claims that he was acting in his personal capacity.

“Attorney general Blanche’s appearances at political events are made in his personal capacity. His appearances are reviewed and cleared by the department’s ethics officials. Travel expenses are reimbursed by the attorney general in accordance with federal law, regulations and policies,” a DOJ spokesperson said.

Federal ethics regulations prohibit officials from taking actions that “create even the appearance of violating the law or ethical standards”, Joseph Tirrell, who was fired as the top ethics official at the justice department last year, wrote in a blogpost earlier this year.
“The question is not merely whether Blanche crossed a technical line. It is whether his appearance made federal law enforcement look like an arm of a partisan campaign,” Tirrell wrote.

“Senior Trump administration law enforcement officials at DoJ, FBI and DHS have yet to be held accountable for their weaponization of prosecutions and legal attacks on candidates or their apparent violations of the Hatch Act, which bans them from using their official positions for political purposes,” Sherman said. “From Blanche’s participation in political rallies to Trump’s attacks on voting to the recent raid on a congresswoman’s home, these relentless attempts to influence the upcoming election are incredibly disturbing and pose a serious threat to our democracy.”

The DoJ’s insertion into electoral politics comes as far-right figures have urged Trump to take the drastic step of seizing voting machines before the election – something he does not have the power to do. The Trump administration has also refused to rule out sending ICE agents to the polls.

A compliant justice department would get rid of a significant guardrail to implementing some of those ideas. As Trump sought to overturn the results of the 2020 election, senior officials in the justice department refused to go along with the idea and threatened to resign en masse. William Barr, the attorney general in 2020, told Trump the claims about election fraud were “bullshit”.

articles.headline: Fake VPN download site steals administrator credentials to give attackers direct access to corporate networks — but delivers official signed software so victims never suspect a thing
keyFacts: Huntress investigators found a fake website that stole WatchGuard VPN credentials from users before providing them with legitimate, signed software.
The fraudulent site collected VPN server addresses, usernames, and passwords to potentially give attackers direct access to corporate networks.
Huntress reported the main deceptive domain was offline by October 13 and advised organizations to reset compromised passwords and enable multifactor authentication.
body: - Fake WatchGuard VPN website steals administrator credentials while delivering legitimate software
- Attackers collected VPN server addresses, usernames, and passwords
- The fraudulent website rejected initial submissions to collect credentials a second time
A fraudulent WatchGuard download website stole VPN login details while supplying the authentic installation package, experts have claimed.
Security investigators at Huntress traced the activity to a lookalike domain that collected connection details before downloading the legitimate client.
The investigation began after suspicious activity involving an administrator working for a managed service provider was detected.
Fake download pages harvest user credentials
Investigators found that the user had searched Bing for a WatchGuard VPN download before visiting a deceptive website designed to resemble the vendor's official download pages.
The website, watchguard-vpn[.]net, offered a purported mobile VPN with SSL download and displayed a form requesting the server address, username, and password.
Those details matched information required by the genuine VPN client, making the request appear consistent with an ordinary installation process.
Submitting the form transmitted the information to a separate domain, watchguard-ssl[.]online, where attackers collected the credentials for potential use against the organization's network.
The malicious script rejected the first submission and cleared the fields, prompting the victim to enter the information again and potentially supplying attackers with multiple password attempts.
Huntress revealed that the operators registered the download domain on August 22, 2026, while the credential collection domain appeared on September 14.
WatchGuard had previously reported the lookalike address in January, although researchers then found no functioning mechanism directing visitors through the fraudulent download process.
Genuine software helps conceal the credential theft
After collecting the second submission, the website initiated a download from WatchGuard's official content delivery network rather than providing a counterfeit installation package.
The file was Mobile VPN with SSL client version 12.11.5, carrying a valid digital signature from WatchGuard Technologies and a timestamp dated November 4, 2025.
Huntress verified that the installer remained unchanged after signing, meaning investigators found no evidence that attackers had modified the legitimate executable.
This approach differs from campaigns that distribute tampered installers or malicious libraries, which endpoint protection products may identify through file inspection.
The authentic download also gives victims little reason to suspect their credentials have already been compromised, since installation can proceed normally afterward.
Huntress found no recorded download from the official server during the investigated incident, suggesting the user might not have completed both credential submissions.
The detection arrived 21 seconds after the malicious website loaded, allowing the security operations team to provide remediation guidance before investigators observed further escalation.
Huntress reported that the main deceptive domain was offline by October 13, although that status does not establish whether associated infrastructure remains active elsewhere.
The attack avoids many malware checks because the fake website steals VPN credentials through the browser before downloading the genuine software.
Organizations should reset compromised passwords, enable multifactor authentication, check for suspicious VPN logins, and direct employees to official software download pages.
